A day after hosting world leaders in Ukraine for the country’s independence day celebrations, president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has taken to social media with a flurry of posts thanking those who sent their best wishes, including Donald Trump. The Ukrainian president appeared to make a pointed nod to one of his most pressing requests, saying Trump’s message of support lifted spirits “much like the sound of a Patriot PAC-3 launch”. The US Patriot air defence system has been instrumental in protecting Ukraine’s cities from Russian attacks, but stocks are running dangerously low. The shortage has been compounded by the US and Israel’s war on Iran, with Patriot interceptors diverted to defend US bases and regional allies in the Middle East, leaving fewer available for Ukraine as Russia continues to launch waves of ballistic missiles. https://www.maitlandmercury.com.au/story.text: Twelve ‌people have been killed and more than a dozen injured in Russian air attacks on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv and ‌the surrounding region, in the sixth day in a row of strikes on the area. Attacks both in Ukraine and Russia continue as efforts are ongoing to find a solution to end the deadliest conflict on the European continent since the World War II, which started with Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022. Eight people were killed and another five wounded in Kyiv, three of them children, and fires broke out in different locations around the capital, emergency service said on the Telegram messaging app. In Boryspil just outside Kyiv, four people were killed and a further 13 injured in an attack that hit a residential building and other sites, Governor Tymur Tkachenko said on Telegram. One of the dead outside Kyiv was an Indian citizen. Russia has been increasing attacks on Ukraine's borders, in addition to energy and logistic facilities, and on Tuesday a fresh strike stopped border crossings into Romania - a member of the European Union and NATO - at Orlivka on ⁠the Danube river. In Russia, a drone attack caused a fire in the port ‌area of Ust-Luga, ​a major export outlet in the northwest. In Russia's Samara region, home to a number of major oil refineries some 800km southeast ‌of Moscow, an air attack damaged civilian facilities, the local governor said on Telegram. Russia and Ukraine deny targeting civilians. ​Reuters could not independently verify ⁠the damage reports. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha wrote on X that Russia's latest attack on Kyiv demonstrated President Vladimir Putin is not interested in peace. Ukraine's top diplomat called for new international sanctions targeting Russia's ability to continue producing ballistic missiles and urged its partners to use frozen Russian assets, particularly those held in the European Union. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday he held ‌a "detailed ​and constructive" call with US President Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and the sides ​were working to ‌finalise dates for their visit to Ukraine aimed at advancing peace efforts. The same day, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Putin the war needed to end for humanity's sake. ‌The Kremlin leader said Moscow was "moving forward along this path". The conflict prompted some NATO members, especially those bordering Russia, to bolster their military capabilities, also in the wake of intensifying drone incidents in the border areas. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP Mississippi Third person arrested in death of Tasia Fortune, as police say hanging was staged Eric Clark, 45, charged with murder as autopsy concludes Fortune was dead days before body discovered in tree Marina Dunbar Sat 26 Sep 2026 13.20 EDT Last modified on Sat 26 Sep 2026 13.21 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A third person has been arrested in the death of 29-year-old Tasia Fortune in Mississippi ’s capital city, while investigators said they had determined the scene where her body was found hanging had been staged. Eric Clark, 45, surrendered to authorities on Friday and was charged with murder, according to the Jackson police department (JPD). Clark was scheduled to make a court appearance on Monday. Police disclosed Friday that an autopsy investigation concluded “the scene and the hanging were staged”. Authorities did not release additional information about the circumstances surrounding Fortune’s killing or why investigators believe the scene was faked. Clark’s arrest comes after two other men, Earnest Lloyd Jr and Jarques Ratliff, were charged with murder in connection with Fortune’s death. The case leading to the arrests of Clark, Lloyd Jr and Ratliff had drawn national attention because of the severity of Fortune’s killing and Mississippi’s history of racist violence and lynchings. Clark, Lloyd Jr, Ratliff are Black, as was Fortune. “The Jackson police department’s robbery-homicide division will continue its investigation until all individuals believed to be involved are held accountable for their actions in connection with Ms Fortune’s death,” a news release shared with multiple news outlets states. Fortune, a mother of four, was discovered on 3 August hanging from a tree behind a vacant home on the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in the western part of Jackson. Investigators have said Fortune was not killed at the location where her body was found. JPD detective Samuel Dukes previously described Fortune’s hanging in court as “staged”, saying investigators believe she was killed somewhere else before her body was placed in a hanging position in the tree on Road of Remembrance. He added investigators determined Fortune had been dead for two to three days before her body was discovered. Police have released few details about the events leading to Fortune’s death. Detectives have interviewed as many as 15 people, according to the police news release. Local TV news station WLBT reported an alleged physical altercation between Lloyd, 25, and Fortune that occurred shortly before her death. Police accused Lloyd of using a black cable cord to hang Fortune, according to WLBT. Ratliff and Lloyd have both reportedly pleaded not guilty. Each has been denied bond. Fortune’s mother, Christy Spivey, has said she was certain her daughter would not have killed herself.
